newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo reports on new septic shock drug.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo reports on new septic shock drug.

text.p: Glaxo-Wellcome presented data on Thursday indicating its experimental septic shock drug 546C88 could alleviate symptoms and restore patient's balance.
Researchers told the International Symposium of Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine in Brussels they would soon be starting large-scale clinical trials of the drug.
There is currently no good treatment for septic shock, which results when infection overwhelms the body. Blood pressure plunges and about half the victims die.
Glaxo estimates half a million patients develop septic shock every year in Europe and North America. Vulnerable people include burn, cancer and surgery patients.
The drug 546C88 is a nitric oxide synthase inhibitor -- it controls overproduction of NO, which is an important factor in regulating blood pressure.

Robert Grover, senior clinical researcher for Glaxo-Wellcome Research and Development, reported results from a study in which about 150 patients with septic shock were given 546C88 intravenously. Another 150 got placebo.
Most of the patients were already on blood pressure-regulating drugs. Using 546C88 reduced the need for those drugs, Glaxo-Wellcome said in a statement.
The drug was also shown to be safe, he said.
Daryl Rees, a clinical pharmacologist at University College London, told the conference that tests in animals showed overproduction of NO led to cardiovascular collapse, organ failure and death.
Using 546C88 reversed the cardiovascular collapse and increased survival from 25 percent to 75 percent.
"This is a significant advance, since it is the first time that a treatment for septic shock has affected survival to such an extent," Rees said.
Glaxo-Wellcome said it was starting a trial using more than 4,000 patients.

Other companies are working on septic shock treatments, as well. Celltech Group Plc and Bayer AG have a joint effort underway and hope to produce late-stage trial data in April. -- Maggie Fox, London Newsroom 44-171-542-8958
